## Welcome to the Course {.unnumbered}

This course introduces engineering students to the principles, tools, and practices of **professional project management**. Whether you are building a bridge, developing software, or managing a manufacturing plant upgrade, the ability to plan, execute, and control projects is one of the most valuable skills an engineer can possess.

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## 🎯 Course Philosophy

This course is built on a simple idea: **Project Management is an engineering discipline**. It requires systematic thinking, quantitative analysis, and structured problem solving — the same skills you use in your technical courses, applied to the management of complex, real-world endeavours.
:::

## What You Will Learn {.unnumbered}

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Part I — Foundations
- ✅ Understand what projects are and why they fail
- ✅ Analyse projects using the systems view and three-sphere model
- ✅ Navigate the five process groups and ten knowledge areas
- ✅ Understand organisational structures, culture, and their impact on PM
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Part II — Planning
- ✅ Build Work Breakdown Structures (WBS)
- ✅ Schedule projects using Gantt charts and CPM
- ✅ Allocate and level resources efficiently
- ✅ Develop realistic project budgets
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Part III — Execution & Control
- ✅ Identify, analyse, and respond to risks
- ✅ Monitor costs using Earned Value Management
- ✅ Implement quality assurance and control processes
- ✅ Manage change and handle project crises
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### Part IV — Modern Approaches
- ✅ Apply Agile and Scrum to engineering projects
- ✅ Lead high-performance project teams
- ✅ Close projects professionally and capture lessons learned
- ✅ Build a personal PM toolkit for your career
:::

:::

## Course Modules at a Glance {.unnumbered}


| # | Module | Key Topics | Key Tool |
|---|--------|-----------|---------|
| 1 | Introduction to PM | Triple Constraint, PMBOK, Why Projects Fail | PM Framework |
| 2 | PM & Engineering Context | Systems View, Four Frames, Org Structures, Culture | Three-Sphere Model |
| 3 | PM Process Groups | 5 Process Groups × 10 Knowledge Areas, PM Methodology | Process–KA Matrix |
| 4 | Project Initiation & Selection | **PV, FV, NPV, IRR, Break-even**, Charter, Stakeholders, Weighted Scoring | Financial Models |
| 5 | Planning & WBS | Scope, Requirements, Deliverables, Change Control | WBS Diagram |
| 6 | Scheduling | Gantt, CPM, PERT, Schedule Compression | Network Diagram |
| 7 | Resource Management | RACI, Levelling, Tuckman, Leadership | Resource Histogram |
| 8 | Risk Management | Identification, FMEA, EMV, Risk Register | Risk Matrix |
| 9 | Cost Management | **EVM (PV, EV, AC, CPI, SPI, EAC)**, Budgeting, Bottom-Up Estimates | EVM S-Curve |
| 10 | Quality Management | QA/QC, PDCA, Ishikawa, ISO 9001 | Control Charts |
| 11 | Agile & Scrum | Sprints, Kanban, Hybrid Approaches | Scrum Board |
| 12 | Project Closure | Handover, Lessons Learned, Benefits Realisation | Closure Report |

: {.striped .hover}

## Course Conventions {.unnumbered}

Throughout this course, you will encounter the following interactive elements:

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## 🎯 Learning Outcomes
These boxes appear at the start of each chapter and list exactly what you will be able to **do** after completing the chapter.
:::

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## 📖 Key Concept
Blue boxes highlight **important definitions and concepts** you must understand.
:::

::: {.callout-warning icon="false"}
## ⚠️ Common Mistake
Yellow boxes warn you about **frequent errors** that engineering students (and even professionals) make.
:::

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## 🏭 Real-World Case Study
Orange boxes present **industry case studies** with analysis questions.
:::

::: {.callout-caution icon="false"}
## ✏️ Exercise
Green exercise boxes contain **practice problems** to test your understanding.
:::

## Prerequisites {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
This course assumes you are comfortable with:

- Basic mathematics (algebra, statistics)
- Reading and interpreting charts and diagrams
- General engineering problem solving
- Spreadsheet software (Excel / Google Sheets)

No prior project management knowledge is required.
:::

---

## References & Standards {.unnumbered}

This course draws on internationally recognised standards and frameworks:

- **PMBOK® Guide** (7th Edition) — Project Management Institute [@pmbok2021]
- **ISO 21500:2021** — Project Management Standard  
- **APM Body of Knowledge** (7th Edition) [@apm2019]
- **Agile Manifesto** [@beck2001agile]
- **PRINCE2** — Projects in Controlled Environments [@prince22017]
